title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: M_{0,3}^! is the extension 1 → Π̂_{0,3} → M_{0,3}^! → Γ_Q → 1, where Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite π_1 of P^1−{0,1,∞} and Γ_Q is (a subgroup containing) Gal(Q̄/Q). This is the arithmetic fundamental group of U_{0,3,Q}, possibly enlarged by the symmetries ρ and σ_∞ of the previous pages.

On the previous page (419) Grothendieck finishes a proof. The automorphisms u_g, for g a solution of his equations (14) and (15) (the 'équation des lacets' and its companions), form a subgroup meeting the inner automorphisms trivially. This gives a canonical partial section over the subgroups N^{!≈}.

This page draws the consequence. Restricting to a subgroup containing Γ_Q gives a canonical section Γ_Q → M_{0,3}^! of the extension. That section actually lands in the normalizer of L_0, the inertia (cusp) subgroup at the point 0. In modern terms it is a section of the decomposition group D_0 = N(L_0). D_0 is an extension of Γ_Q by L_0 ≅ Ẑ(1).

Such sections, up to L_0-conjugacy, form a torsor under H^1(Γ_Q, Ẑ(1)) = (Q^*)^∧ (Kummer theory). The sections coming from rational tangential base points at 0 are indexed by nonzero elements of the line m_0/m_0^2. Here m_0 is the maximal ideal of the local ring at 0 of the compactification Û_{0,3,Q} = P^1_Q.

Grothendieck conjectures that his canonical section is the one attached to a well-determined uniformizer class in m_0/m_0^2, and asks which one. His heuristic is integrality: require the class to be a basis over Z, not just over Q, in the model over the integers. This pins the class down up to sign, giving z or −z.

The ambiguity is genuine. The two sections differ by the Kummer character of −1, i.e. the quadratic character Γ_Q → μ_2 ⊂ Ẑ(1) which is nontrivial on complex conjugation. He leaves the question open ('Mais est-ce bien le bon? Il faudrait y revenir!').

The next page (420) uses the section to write M^{!≈}_{0,3} as a semidirect product M^{!≈}(0)·Π̂_{0,3}. There every element is int(f^{-1})∘u_g, matching his earlier parametrization u_{g,f} = u_{α,β,f}.
errors: No outright error. The identification of the canonical section with a tangential section is stated as something to be checked, not proved.

The Z-integrality criterion only reduces the choice to ±z. Which sign matches the section defined by (14)/(15) and the symmetries ρ, σ_∞ is left undetermined. With symmetry constraints involving 1−z, the other sign could plausibly be the right one, so the heuristic is incomplete.

ideas.what: Canonical section of π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}/Q) → Γ_Q landing in the normalizer of the inertia group at 0, obtained from solutions of the loop equations
ideas.modern_name: Galois section attached to a tangential base point (cuspidal section, decomposition group at a cusp)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points'); Ihara; Anderson; also Nakamura on cuspidal sections
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's 1983 letter to Faltings mentions packets of sections attached to points at infinity (cusps); exact tangential formulation unsure

ideas.what: Sections in the normalizer of L_0 are parametrized by elements of m_0/m_0^2 (uniformizer classes), i.e. a torsor under Kummer classes
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points ↔ nonzero tangent vectors; Kummer torsor H^1(Γ_Q, Ẑ(1))

ideas.what: Normalizing the tangent vector by integrality over Z (basis of m_0/m_0^2 over Z), hence ±z
ideas.modern_name: Integral (unit) tangential base point 01→ (tangent vector d/dz) versus tangent vector −1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne 1989 (tangential base points over Z), Ihara

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks which of the two integral tangential base points at 0 (z or −z) gives his canonical section, the one characterized by solutions of his loop equations (14)/(15) and the S_3-type symmetries. He never settles it on this page.
missed.quote: ce serait en fait le choix correspondant à l'uniformisante z, ou −z. Mais est-ce bien le bon? Il faudrait y revenir!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The sign question corresponds to a twist by the quadratic Kummer character of −1. It parallels the known delicacy of choosing tangential base points compatibly with GT symmetries. This is now understood in the literature (Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps), so it is historically interesting but not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The page shows Grothendieck independently arriving at tangential base points and their Z-normalization from his GT-type loop equations. This anticipates or parallels Deligne's 1989 formalism, but the content itself is now standard.
transcription_corrections: 'point 0 de M̂_{0,3 Q}': the image shows the compactified M̂_{0,3,Q}, identified two lines later with Û_{0,3,Q} = P^1_Q.
'{+bien+} déterminée': 'bien' is an insertion above 'déterminée' ('bien déterminée').
'normalisateurs[?]': the reading 'normalisateurs de L_0' fits the mathematics.
'un [?] un élément': the illegible word is a short scribble, possibly struck through. The sense is 'détermine un élément de m_0/m_0^2 au signe près'.
